description: World Population Prospects is the official series of United Nations population estimates and projections prepared by the Population Division of the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs. The home page read on 2026-09-28 describes the 2024 revision, the twenty-eighth edition, with estimates from 1950 to the present for 237 countries or areas built from 1,910 national censuses, vital registration and 3,189 sample surveys, and projections to 2100 that span a range of plausible outcomes. Results come as Excel files of key demographic indicators by country, region, income group and SDG region, as CSV files for bulk download, and through a Data Portal with an open API; since 2022 the series uses one-year intervals of age and time, and special aggregates regroup countries. Coverage is global at country level. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): UN terms of use: personal, non-commercial use (the WPP site gives no separate open licence). Access is free of charge. Caveats: values are national, not subnational, projections carry uncertainty, and each revision replaces earlier numbers. It supports exposure and planning studies, such as scaling infrastructure demand or people exposed to hazards under projected population to 2050. Related records: the US Census International Database gives alternative projections, and GHSL gives gridded population.
